newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Unitrans buys Namibian freight firm.
newsitem.headline: Unitrans buys Namibian freight firm.

text.p: South Africa's Unitrans Ltd said on Tuesday it had bought Namibian freight carrying firm Road Runners for 13 million rand.
The move gives Unitrans a foothold in Namibia, the only southern African country in which it did not yet have a presence.

Unitrans chief executive Eduardo Gutierrez-Garcia said that Namibian government schemes to improve transportation in the large and mostly arid country meant Road Runners was poised for a bright future.

"The considerable effort that Namibia is making in developing its road infrastructure to facilitate communications with all the bordering countries will result in the movement of greater volumes of goods, from which Road Runners stands to benefit," he said in a statement.
Road Runners, with a fleet of 50 vehicles, has depots in Walvis Bay, Windhoek and Grootfontein.
Its main operations are fuel distribution for oil companies, long distance cross-border freight and daily services between Namibia and Cape Town.
The business will continue to be run by former owner Jacques Maree.
